props.title: Manufacture of oxygenated organic compounds

props.name: basic zinc chromate (methanol catalyst of the preliminary operation)

evidence.note: 'non oxide' is the text layer of 'monoxide'
evidence.quote: Mixtures of carbon non oxide or carbon dioxide and hydrogen Or gases containing such mixtures may be passed through a reaction chamber containing zinc oxide or basic zinc chromate or other catalysts or catalyst mix tures capable of producing methyl alcohol,

props.name: iron and cobalt in the acid radicle: ferrites, ferrates, cobaltites, cobaltates
props.description: catalysts containing iron or cobalt in the acid radicle of a salt, particularly salts of sodium, potassium, barium, calcium, magnesium and aluminium ("metallate catalysts")

evidence.quote: I have now found that cobalt and iron may be present in the catalyst or catalyst mixture in the form of a salt in which the iron Or Cobalt is pres ent in the acid radicle, and that such use of iron and cobalt tends to direct the reaction towards the production of oxygenated compounds,
For example they may be present in the form of ferrites, ferrates, cobaltites and CO baltates, and particularly in the form of such salts of the alkali and alkaline earth metals,

props.name: zinc oxide (methanol catalyst of the preliminary operation)

evidence.note: 'non oxide' is the text layer of 'monoxide'
evidence.quote: Mixtures of carbon non oxide or carbon dioxide and hydrogen Or gases containing such mixtures may be passed through a reaction chamber containing zinc oxide or basic zinc chromate or other catalysts or catalyst mix tures capable of producing methyl alcohol,

props.name: copper, even in small proportions, favourable

evidence.quote: may be employed according to the present invention in conjunction with copper, the presence of the copper, even in Small proportions, exercising a favourable influence upon the re action.
the reaction may be carried out in copper vessels or in copper lined vessels.

props.statement: The catalysts or catalyst mixtures may be used in conjunction with copper, whose presence even in small proportions exercises a favourable influence on the reaction; alternatively or in addition the reaction may be carried out in copper or copper-lined vessels.

props.name: metallates may be combined with Zn, Mg, Ca, Al, Cr, Mo, V, Mn, W or U

evidence.quote: catalysts in admixture or in association with zinc, magnesium, calcium, aluminium, chromium, mo lybdenum, vanadium, manganese, tungsten or uranium, or with two or more of these metals,

props.statement: The metallate catalysts may be employed in admixture or association with zinc, magnesium, calcium, aluminium, chromium, molybdenum, vanadium, manganese, tungsten or uranium, or with two or more of them (e.g. zinc and vanadium, zinc and molybdenum, chromium and manganese), the other metals being present as metals, oxides or other compounds.

props.name: iron and cobalt held deleterious to oxygenates (prior view)

evidence.quote: in the hydrogenation of oxides Or carbon it has been considered that the presence of these metals or compounds containing them has been productive of hydrocarbons such as methane and deleterious to the production of oxy genated Organic compounds.

props.note: the view held in the art, which the patent argues against
props.statement: Iron and cobalt are well known hydrogenating catalysts, but in the hydrogenation of oxides of carbon their presence, or that of their compounds, has been considered productive of hydrocarbons such as methane and deleterious to the production of oxygenated organic compounds.

props.name: copper chambers advantageous; alloy steels usable

evidence.quote: the use of copper chambers or copper lined chambers present ad vantages, but steel chambers, and particularly steeel containing molybdenum, tungsten, man ganese, cobalt, nickel or the like may also be used.

props.statement: The reactions may be carried out in any suitable chamber; copper or copper-lined chambers present advantages, but steel chambers, particularly steel containing molybdenum, tungsten, manganese, cobalt, nickel or the like, may also be used.

props.name: methanol made in a preliminary stage over ZnO or basic zinc chromate, passed directly over the metallates

evidence.quote: The methyl alcohol or other compound may be prepared in a preliminary Operation con tinuously with its use according to the present invention for the production of higher oxygenated organic compounds.

props.statement: The methyl alcohol may be prepared in a preliminary operation continuously with its use: carbon monoxide or dioxide and hydrogen are passed over zinc oxide, basic zinc chromate or other methanol catalysts, and the resulting gases or vapours passed directly over the catalysts of the invention.

props.name: catalytic hydrogenation of oxides of carbon to oxygenated organic compounds
props.description: product slate of higher oxygenated compounds (e.g. acetaldehyde, ethyl and propyl alcohol, acetone, aliphatic acids); no equation is given

evidence.quote: oxygenated organic compounds are produced by the catalytic hydrogenation of oxides of carbon in presence of iron and cobalt in the form of com pounds containing these metals in the acid radicle.

props.name: conversion of methanol into higher oxygenated compounds
props.description: methanol, with or without CO, CO2 and/or H2, converted into ethyl alcohol, acetaldehyde, acetic acid etc.; no equation is given

evidence.quote: In this modification of the invention methyl alcohol, for example, may be converted into compounds of a higher order, for example into ethyl alcohol, acetaldehyde, acetic acid etc.
